newsitem.title: CHINA: China says farm land eroded by urbanisation.
newsitem.headline: China says farm land eroded by urbanisation.

text.p: China's valuable arable land is being eroded by rapid urbanisation and rampant use by non-farm projects, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
China's arable land declined by 1.97 million hectares between 1986 and 1995 because of urban expansion and land taken by industry, it quoted the State Land Administration as saying.
A survey by the administration found that the combined areas of China's 31 major cities rose by 50.2 percent over the period, the newspaper said.
The arable area also declined because many regional governments have rushed to set up new development zones to try to attract investment and boost their local economies.
In 1995 alone, the State Land Administration uncovered 133,320 hectares of farm land left to waste after being taken over by deveopers.
Land used by farmers to build new houses reached 3.399 million hectares in 1995, the Economic Daily said.
